blocks.text: **The problem.** Given the `head` of a **sorted** linked list, delete every duplicate so each value appears only once. Return the list, still sorted.

blocks.alt: Before: 1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3. The second 1 and the second 3 are duplicates. After: 1 -> 2 -> 3.

blocks.code:
Input:  head = [1, 1, 2]
Output: [1, 2]

Input:  head = [1, 1, 2, 3, 3]
Output: [1, 2, 3]

blocks.text: The word **sorted** is the hint. In a sorted list, all copies of a value sit **next to each other**.
1. Brute force: for every node, delete its later copies
Pretend the list isn't sorted. For each node, run a second pointer over the rest of the list and unlink every later node with the same value.
**Time O(n²), space O(1).** Correct even for unsorted lists — but each node scans everything after it.
2. Optimal: remember the values you've seen
Walk once with a **hash set** of values already kept. If the next node's value is in the set, unlink it; otherwise add the value and move on.
**Time O(n), space O(n).** One pass — but the set can grow as large as the list, and it still ignores the fact that the list is sorted.
3. Best solution: compare each node with its neighbour

Because the list is sorted, a duplicate can only be the **very next** node. So look at `curr` and `curr.next`: if they're equal, skip the next node (and **stay** on curr — the node after might be another copy). If they differ, move on.

blocks.alt: 1 -> 1 -> 1 -> 2: curr sits on the first 1. The next node is also 1, so curr.next skips over it. curr stays put because the following node is another 1.
blocks.caption: Copies are always neighbours, so one comparison per node is enough.
Try a run of three equal values: curr stays put until the run is gone.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(1).** One pass, one pointer.

blocks.alt: Brute force: O(n²) time, O(1) space. Optimal: O(n) time, O(n) space. Best: O(n) time, O(1) space.

blocks.text: A harder follow-up removes **every** node that has a duplicate (`[1, 1, 2, 3, 3]` → `[2]`). That one needs a dummy node, because the head itself may disappear.
